title: Long video and memory: chunks, tiled decode, and what truly helps

questions.q: Your LTX run dies on the first sampling step. Which fix can work?
options: Lower the length or the picture size
VAEDecodeTiled with smaller tiles
A larger temporal overlap
More sampling steps
questions.answer: Lower the length or the picture size
questions.why: Sampling runs before decoding. Tile settings act only at the decode node, so only fewer tokens can help.

questions.q: Why does VAEDecodeTiled do nothing useful on H3?
options: H3's decode_tiled ignores the tile settings and calls decode, which already chunks internally
H3's latents are too small
H3 has no VAE
It needs a higher overlap
questions.answer: H3's decode_tiled ignores the tile settings and calls decode, which already chunks internally
questions.why: comfy/ldm/minimax/vae.py defines decode_tiled(self, z, **kwargs) as return self.decode(z).

questions.q: With a temporal tile, what happens to LTX's decode estimate as the clip gets longer?
options: It stops growing, because the estimate is for one tile
It grows in line with the frames
It grows with the square of the frames
It falls
questions.answer: It stops growing, because the estimate is for one tile
questions.why: _tile_bounded_shape clamps the shape to one tile. The lab shows 18.7 GiB at 121, 241 and 481 frames with temporal tile 8.

questions.q: A chain of clips replaces one long render. What gets better, and what's the new cost?
options: Peak sampler memory stays at one clip's; the cost moves to seams and drift between clips
Everything gets better, with no new cost
Peak memory is the sum of all clips
It uses less total work and no seams
questions.answer: Peak sampler memory stays at one clip's; the cost moves to seams and drift between clips
questions.why: Each clip samples alone, so peak stays the same. Every join can show, and each clip starts from a generated frame.

questions.q: 60 s at 1920 x 1088 finishes sampling and decoding, then the machine runs out of RAM. What's a sensible fix?
options: Save clips to disk and join files, since the frames alone are 33.6 GiB as float32
Use a smaller tile
Lower the CFG
Change the sampler
questions.answer: Save clips to disk and join files, since the frames alone are 33.6 GiB as float32
questions.why: An IMAGE is 3 x 4 bytes a pixel. RAM here has nothing to do with the VAE's tiles or with the sampler.

questions.q: Why does the join graph take frames from index 1 of the second clip?
options: Clip 2 begins on clip 1's last frame, so keeping it twice would stutter
Index 0 is always black
ImageBatch requires it
The video codec can't start at 0
questions.answer: Clip 2 begins on clip 1's last frame, so keeping it twice would stutter
questions.why: ImageFromBatch with batch_index 1 and length 8 drops the repeated first frame, so 9 + 8 = 17 frames.
